ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The primary coil of an ideal transformer is connected to an AC power source with $\mathrm{u}=220\sqrt{2}\mathrm{sin}\pi t$ (V), and the secondary coil is connected to a load resistor with R $=55\Omega$. The turns ratio of the primary to secondary coil is 2:1. The ammeter and voltmeter are both ideal instruments.

1. Find the reading of the voltmeter.
2. Find the reading of the ammeter.
3. Find the input power of the primary coil.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The primary coil of an ideal transformer is connected to an AC power source with $\mathrm{u}=220\sqrt{2}\mathrm{sin}\pi t$ (V), and the secondary coil is connected to a load resistor with R $=55\Omega$. The turns ratio of the primary to secondary coil is 2:1. The ammeter and voltmeter are both ideal instruments. 1. Find the reading of the voltmeter. 2. Find the reading of the ammeter. 3. Find the input power of the primary coil.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The diagram shows an AC source labeled u on the left connected to the primary side of a transformer. An ammeter A is placed in series in the primary circuit. On the right, the secondary coil is connected across two vertical terminals; a resistor labeled R is connected between these terminals, and an ideal voltmeter V is also connected between the same two terminals, so the resistor and voltmeter are in parallel across the secondary output. Reasoning: The source voltage is u = 220√2 sin(πt) V, so its RMS value is U1 = 220 V. For an ideal transformer, U1/U2 = N1/N2. The turns ratio is N1:N2 = 2:1, hence U2 = U1 × (N2/N1) = 220 × 1/2 = 110 V. Since the ideal voltmeter is connected across the secondary terminals and draws no current, its reading is 110 V. The load resistor is R = 55 Ω, so the secondary current through the resistor is I2 = U2/R = 110/55 = 2 A. For an ideal transformer, I1/I2 = N2/N1 = 1/2, so I1 = 1 A. This is the ammeter reading because the ammeter is in series with the primary circuit. The load is purely resistive and the transformer is ideal, so input power equals output power. P_in = U1 I1 = 220 × 1 = 220 W, also equal to U2 I2 = 110 × 2 = 220 W.
